healthcareSystem: Basic public healthcare system. Princess Margaret Hospital in Roseau is the main facility. A few private clinics supplement public care. Rural areas have health centers with limited capabilities.
qualityNotes: Healthcare is basic but functional for routine issues. Princess Margaret Hospital handles emergencies. English is spoken everywhere. Limited specialist care — serious conditions require evacuation to Martinique, Guadeloupe, or Barbados.
pharmacyHours: Pharmacies open 8am-5pm weekdays, 8am-1pm Saturday. Limited evening and Sunday availability.
pharmacyTips: Pharmacies in Roseau and Portsmouth are reasonably stocked for basic medications. English is spoken everywhere. Bring specialty medications from home. Limited options outside the two main towns.
prescriptionRules: Prescriptions required for controlled substances. English-speaking country so communication is easy. Many basic medications available OTC.

restrictedMeds.name: Narcotic medications
restrictedMeds.note: Carry a doctor's letter. Keep in original packaging.

restrictedMeds.name: Cannabis products
restrictedMeds.note: Cannabis is illegal in Dominica. Do not bring CBD or THC products.

bringDocumentation: Carry a doctor's letter listing all prescription medications. Keep medications in original labeled containers. English documentation is accepted.

travelInsurance.tips: Strongly recommended. Medical evacuation to Martinique, Guadeloupe, or Barbados may be needed for serious conditions. Ensure coverage includes hiking (Waitukubuli Trail), diving, and adventure activities.

vaccinations.notes: Yellow fever certificate required if arriving from an endemic country. Dengue risk exists — use insect repellent. No malaria in Dominica.

waterNotes: Tap water is generally safe in Roseau and major towns. Dominica has abundant freshwater from its volcanic rivers. In remote areas, use bottled water to be safe. Resort water is safe.
foodSafetyTips: Food at restaurants is generally safe. Fresh seafood and local produce are excellent. Be cautious with reef fish due to ciguatera risk — ask locals about safe species. Mountain chicken (frog legs, the national dish) is now rare and protected.
medicalTourismNote: Dominica is not a medical tourism destination. The island promotes wellness tourism (hot springs, nature therapy). For medical care, patients travel to Martinique, Guadeloupe, or Barbados.
metaDescription: Health guide for Dominica: emergency numbers, pharmacy tips, restricted medications, vaccinations, safe tap water, and insurance advice.

hospitals.name: Princess Margaret Hospital
hospitals.notes: Main and largest hospital in Dominica. Emergency department. Handles most medical situations. English-speaking staff.

hospitals.name: Portsmouth Hospital
hospitals.nearTouristArea: Portsmouth (near Cabrits National Park and cruise port)
hospitals.notes: Second hospital on the island. Basic emergency care. Serves the northern part of the island.

hospitals.name: Marigot Hospital
hospitals.notes: Small district hospital. Basic care for the east coast.

hospitals.name: Ross University Medical Clinic
hospitals.notes: Associated with Ross University School of Medicine. Good standard of care when available.

dentalCare.availability: Limited dental care in Roseau. Very few dentists on the island.
dentalCare.notes: A few private dental practitioners in Roseau. English-speaking. Equipment may be basic.
dentalCare.emergencyTip: Princess Margaret Hospital has dental referral capabilities. Private dental offices in Roseau for non-emergency care.

mentalHealth.englishTherapists: Very limited. A few counselors in Roseau. English is the official language.
mentalHealth.notes: Mental health services are limited on the island. Bring all psychiatric medications from home.

accessibilityInfo.overview: Accessibility is very limited. Dominica is a mountainous, rugged island. Most attractions involve hiking and uneven terrain.
accessibilityInfo.hospitalAccess: Princess Margaret Hospital has basic wheelchair access.
accessibilityInfo.transport: No accessible public transport. Roads are steep and winding. Private taxi transfers available.
accessibilityInfo.tips: Dominica is nicknamed the 'Nature Island' and is very challenging for mobility-impaired travelers. The Waitukubuli Trail and most waterfalls require strenuous hiking. Some coastal accommodations may be more accessible. Confirm in advance.

covidStatus.entryRequirements: No COVID testing or vaccination requirements for entry as of 2026.
covidStatus.notes: Dengue, hiking injuries, and hurricane season (June-November) are more relevant health concerns.

insuranceClaimProcess: Hospitals require upfront payment (Eastern Caribbean Dollars or USD accepted). Keep all receipts. English documentation provided.

commonCosts.note: Estimated typical out-of-pocket costs. Local currency is Eastern Caribbean Dollar (XCD). USD widely accepted.

medicalEvacuation.note: Medical evacuation insurance is strongly recommended. Martinique and Guadeloupe (French overseas departments) are the closest destinations with good hospitals and are a short flight away.

drugNameMap.note: Both Commonwealth and US brands available.
